statements.new_statement_en: The state should not create or fund new heritage centers for particular communities or movements — Tunisian, Moroccan, Chabad — even if their traditions are less well preserved.

reason: Bills are heritage bodies, mostly ethnic communities but also Chabad and WWII fighters (about a quarter of weight); widen 'communities' to 'communities or movements'. Bill 5 is Diaspora tuition.

statements.new_statement_en: Israel should give foreign workers and asylum seekers fewer rights — to stay, to work, to social benefits — even if their living conditions worsen.

reason: Heaviest bills are Basic Laws on immigration and asylum-seeker status, not pensions; the statement must cover residence and work rights besides social benefits.
Weighty bills are judicial selection, override clause, constitutional court and judges' oversight: exactly politicians' power over courts. Minimum-sentence and Law of Return bills are light.
Most weight is regularizing young settlements, outposts, electricity and tax benefits in Judea and Samaria. Bill 1 is an eastern-border tax bill only partly in the West Bank.
Nearly all bills ease early withdrawal from study funds, provident funds and soldier savings. Deposit-ceiling and terror-sanction bills are light and off.

statements.new_statement_en: Appointments to senior state posts should be vetted by an independent committee, even if this limits politicians' choice.

reason: Dominant bill moves the judges' ombudsman appointment toward the Knesset, not ministers; replace 'ministers' with 'politicians' so it covers all weighty appointment bills.
Bills regulate contract terms for buyers, workers, consumers, athletes, and cap lawyer fees, or deregulate tariffs: state intervention in contracts to protect the weaker party.
Most weight denies allowances, legal aid, health perks and prison privileges to terrorists and families. Draft-evasion, flag and senior-official bills are off but a minority.

split.plus_en: An indicted prime minister or minister keeps office and is shielded from investigation or removal
split.minus_en: An indicted prime minister or minister must leave office
split.statement_en: A person who has been indicted should not be allowed to head the government, even if a court has not yet found them guilty.

split.name_en: Checks on the prime minister's power
split.plus_en: The prime minister decides more alone (appointments, dismissals, inquiries, agreements)
split.minus_en: The prime minister's decisions need more approval or are bound by rules
split.statement_en: The prime minister should have less freedom to act alone, for example to replace senior officials or refuse a state inquiry, even if governing slows.

reason: Indictment bills carry about a third of weight; the rest is deputy PM, inquiries, dismissals, referendums. Two distinct issues. Bill 1 unidentified, drugs and budget bills left out.
Bills expand study grants, school meals, free tuition, student travel and benefits for soldier and reservist students: more state support for students and pupils.

statements.new_statement_en: Every citizen should be able to vote easily — including soldiers, students and those who did not serve — even if elections cost more to run.

reason: Bills ease voting (aircrew, students, address, nursing homes, abroad) and widen or narrow the franchise (service condition). Current text bundles two ideas; restate as one: easy voting for all.
Bills give municipalities powers over guards, Shabbat transport and business hours, water, shelters, enforcement and planning. Synagogue, conversion and place-name bills are off but minor.
Weighty bills ban electricity cut-offs and travel bans for small debts, limit seizures, defer reservists' payments, or speed collection: creditors' versus debtors' powers, as stated.
